subject: Enclave readiness — procurement gating and isolation constraints (post-call synthesis)
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@medsecure.com>, Bob Li <bob.li@medsecure.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Jul 2028 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Enclave readiness — procurement gating and isolation constraints (post-call synthesis)

Alice / Bob — thanks again for the time today. Quick synth of what we heard on the call and proposed next steps so everyone's aligned. If anything below is off, flag it and I'll update.

Summary of customer goals / drivers
- Regulated inference: Must process PHI and patient identifiers for your analytics pipeline in a way that meets your audit and data residency requirements.
- Air-gapped posture desired for outbound network egress; limited controlled egress for updates/metrics under legal review.
- Procurement timeline: procurement + legal have a June procurement window (you called it the "Q3 procurement gate") and want an internal tech + cost binder for approvals this quarter.

Key constraints we captured
- Network: No public internet access from the inference enclave. Outbound only via a customer-controlled proxy whitelisted IPs (you called this the "approved egress relay").
- Data residency: All inference logs and KV caches must remain in the customer VPC and be encrypted with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM).
- Hardware: Preference for dedicated GPU nodes (A100/Trn equivalent) with strict physical isolation; possibility of an on-prem appliance later.
- Auditability: SOC2 evidence + per-request audit trail (token-level) required for compliance pack.

Open gating questions for procurement/legal (items you said we should help document)
1) Contractual language for limited telemetry: what telemetry can Redwood keep by default, and where do we provide an opt-out (per-tenant telemetry flag).
2) Data deletion SLAs: target retention 30 days by default, ability to sign SLO for immediate purge on contract termination.
3) Export controls: any required export or cross-border clauses for model weights/updates?

Technical asks we committed to
- Deliver an isolation matrix mapping Redwood components to customer-owned network zones (attached: isolation-matrix-v1.xlsx).
- Provide a Private deployment diagram showing egress patterns and KMS flow (attached: redwood-private-arch-diagram.pdf).
- Host a security deep-dive with your infosec team next week (proposed times below).

Proposed next steps & owners
- Rafael: Send the populated isolation matrix (today).
- Ben: Prepare a short technical note on how KV cache and prefix caching operate in an isolated VPC (by Tue 2028-07-31).
- Neha: Draft suggested contract language for telemetry and retention that procurement/legal can review (by Thu 2028-08-02).
- Alice / Bob: Share the name(s) and contact of the procurement and infosec leads for scheduling deep-dive (requested by EOD Mon).

Proposed meeting slots for security deep-dive (30–45m)
- Tue 2028-07-31 09:00–09:45 PT
- Tue 2028-07-31 14:00–14:45 PT
- Wed 2028-08-01 11:00–11:45 PT

Attachments: isolation-matrix-v1.xlsx (matrix of network zones & required controls), redwood-private-arch-diagram.pdf (high-level flow), procurement-checklist-msigned.docx (template).

Thanks — Rafael

Subject: Re: Enclave readiness — procurement gating and isolation constraints (post-call synthesis)

Thanks Rafael — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Egress model: We cannot allow any outbound traffic that is not proxied through our in-house relay. That relay will perform TLS inspection and will only allow traffic to whitelisted destinations. Can you confirm whether Redwood needs any direct outbound (e.g., model update pulls) or if we can support periodic pulls from our relay?

2) Telemetry: Infosec is comfortable with an aggregate success/failure metric but will not allow request-level payload telemetry to leave the VPC. We will review your suggested language on opt-out, but please assume default: no request payload leaves.

3) Procurement: Our procurement lead (Carmen Reyes, carmen.reyes@medsecure.com) is on copy for contracting questions — she'll expect a one-page summary covering security controls, SOC2 artifacts you'll provide, and licensing model. Can you produce that by Wed?

We can do the security deep-dive Tue 2028-07-31 14:00 PT — that slot works for our infosec. I'll add Carmen to the next thread.

-Alice
Alice Nguyen
CTO, MedSecure

Quick technical note to clarify Rafael's KV/cache point for the deep-dive:
- KV cache: In Redwood Private we keep the KV cache inside the customer's VPC; the cache lifecycle can be controlled via an API (expire/purge) and we can add an automated purge hook on termination.
- Model updates: We can support outbound pulls initiated from inside the customer VPC (pulls via your approved egress relay). If you prefer push (Redwood-initiated), that requires an allowlist and inbound coordination — given the air-gap preference, pull is the recommended pattern.
- Telemetry: We can provide aggregated health metrics via a sidecar that pushes only aggregate counters (no payloads). For auditing, per-request audit records can be stored only in the VPC and made available via S3 URI to your auditors; Redwood will not copy payloads outside unless explicitly contractually allowed.

I'll bring a short diagram to the Tue deep-dive showing the pull flow and the audit-store pattern.

-ben
Ben Carter

- One-page security + SOC2 artifact summary tailored for procurement (Neha) — target: Wed 2028-08-01.

2) Confirm acceptable telemetry aggregate set (we'll propose low-cardinality counters).
3) Procurement sign-off on the one-page summary — if positive, we'll follow with a standard SOW + procurement checklist for countersign.

If there are other items to add to the agenda, call them out now and we'll include them. Otherwise, we'll see you Tue.
